title: Localized consent banner states the required disclosures

claim.statement: The rendered consent banner text for each shipped locale states (1) what data is collected or why, (2) that third parties such as analytics or advertising partners receive it, and (3) how the visitor can refuse or withdraw consent.

question.instructions: The state is the visible text of a website consent banner in any language. Which option describes it?

criteria.A: it states the purpose of data collection, AND names third parties or partners who receive data, AND tells the visitor how to refuse or withdraw consent
criteria.B: at least one of those three disclosures is missing

notes: SUPERSEDED (kept for the record, not assurance-eligible): Laya scored this three-disclosure rule at chance. The rule is now decomposed into one single-condition Laya rubric per disclosure: RUB-S1-CONSENT-STATES-PURPOSE, RUB-S1-CONSENT-NAMES-THIRD-PARTIES and RUB-S1-CONSENT-EXPLAINS-WITHDRAWAL (laya-consent-*.rubric.json); the banner conforms when all three VERIFY. Those were measured too and none is assurance-eligible, so this check has no assurance-eligible backend yet. Do not bind new claims to this rubric.

Measured on the pinned checkpoint, CPU fp32, eval mode, one state per forward pass: formulation `choice2_neutral`, held-out accuracy 0.514 (n=181); ECE (15 bins) 0.167 raw logits, 0.167 at the checkpoint's shipped temperature, 0.005 at the fitted temperature 20; at verify 0.85 / refute 0.85, coverage 0.000 (VERIFIED 0, REFUTED 0, INCONCLUSIVE 181) with precision n/a. Calibration split ECE after fitting 0.078 (n=179). Dataset: test/fixtures/system1-calibration/multilingual-consent-banner/ (report: docs/calibration/system1-calibration-report.md).

Formulations tried (held-out accuracy at fitted T): choice3_verbatim 0.381, choice3_tight 0.508, choice2_neutral 0.514, noul_tight 0.442. Controls at the fitted T: CTL-CONSENT-DE-COMPLETE VERIFIED->INCONCLUSIVE (p=0.514); CTL-CONSENT-ES-NO-WITHDRAW REFUTED->INCONCLUSIVE (p=0.505); CTL-CONSENT-JA-NO-THIRD-PARTY REFUTED->INCONCLUSIVE (p=0.503). Replay: 9 runs per control (6 in fresh processes), max thresholded-probability delta 4.16e-06, max logit delta 0.000299; epsilon is 10x the larger of the measured delta and the delta implied by the worst logit wobble seen on any checkpoint (2.99e-4, laya-multilingual under concurrent CPU load), rounded up.

Temperature semantics: `calibration.temperature` replaces the checkpoint's own temperature for this question's (type, option count) bucket, i.e. probabilities are softmax(option logits / T); a runner sets agent.temperature_by_options[temp_bucket] = T and passes no `lang`, so lang_temperatures cannot override it. `measured_ece` is the larger of the calibration-split (in-sample) and held-out test-split ECE at the fitted temperature.
The fitted temperature sits at the schema's upper bound (20): NLL keeps falling as T grows, i.e. the logits carry no usable signal for this rule and the best calibration is a flat 0.5.

Not assurance-eligible: controls land on the wrong status: CTL-CONSENT-DE-COMPLETE, CTL-CONSENT-ES-NO-WITHDRAW, CTL-CONSENT-JA-NO-THIRD-PARTY; no held-out item clears either threshold (coverage 0). Thresholds were not lowered to compensate; this rubric may back diagnostic runs only until a re-authored version measures inside the bar.
Checkpoint is pinned to laya-multilingual; Router auto-selection is not used because a mostly-English banner would route to the English checkpoint and change the model under test per input.
This checks that disclosures are stated, not that the wording satisfies any particular law; legal sufficiency is out of scope for a System One rubric.

Two-option form: there is no 'not a banner' option, so text that is not a consent banner (it states none of the disclosures) maps to B and can REFUTE; the extractor and locator, not the model, are what establish that the input is the banner.
